cases.title: Stage 2 Excellent SQL Conditional Update + Idempotent Webhook Adaptation
cases.accepted_alternatives: Relational atomic conditional UPDATE + async pending checkout.
cases.critical_issue_handling: Addresses p95 <= 100ms, 4x out-of-order webhooks, TTL cleanup, and load/replay testing.
cases.explanation: Complete architectural adaptation preserving PostgreSQL invariants and addressing hot SKU contention, out-of-order webhooks, TTL leaks, and tests.

part_a.initial_approach: Use atomic conditional UPDATE WHERE stock >= qty with unique request_id idempotency key and bounded payment timeout.
part_a.data_and_concurrency: Keep PostgreSQL transaction short around stock reservation while calling payment outside row locks.
part_a.initial_tradeoffs: Slightly higher baseline complexity traded for strong pool efficiency.

part_b.updated_approach: Move to pending checkout reservation via short atomic conditional UPDATE releasing DB connections before async payment webhook, plus unique processed_events table and monotonic state transitions.
part_b.what_changes: Eliminate external payment HTTP wait inside transactions to meet p95 <= 100ms at 500 req/s and shard hot SKU contention.
part_b.what_stays_unchanged: PostgreSQL remains authoritative source of truth with zero overselling invariant and unique idempotency constraint.
part_b.tradeoffs: Accept eventual payment confirmation lag and orphaned reservation reaper complexity in exchange for sub-100ms p95 throughput.
part_b.risks_and_failures: Abandoned reservations reaped via TTL job; protect connection pool with 429 backpressure; alert on p95 latency/lock waits with canary rollback.
part_b.validation_and_testing: 500 req/s hot-SKU concurrent load test verifying zero negative stock; replay 4x duplicate out-of-order webhooks; inject TTL expiry timeout; assert DB pool cap.

part_a.data_and_concurrency: Atomic order row creation + bounded gateway timeout.
part_a.initial_tradeoffs: Simpler PostgreSQL-only design trades lower burst ceiling.

part_b.updated_approach: Shift hot-SKU reservation to Redis atomic DECR Lua script with TTL and async worker reconciliation; track webhook event_id uniquely with monotonic state machine transitions.
part_b.what_changes: Replace hot SQL row locks with sub-millisecond Redis atomic decrements to satisfy <=100ms p95 at 500 req/sec.
part_b.what_stays_unchanged: Zero overselling guarantee and PostgreSQL authoritative order ledger stay unchanged.
part_b.tradeoffs: Trades strong immediate cache-DB consistency for throughput, accepting cache drift reconciliation overhead.
part_b.risks_and_failures: TTL reaper releases orphaned holds; monitor Redis-DB drift, pool saturation, p95 latency alerts, and canary feature-flag rollback.
part_b.validation_and_testing: Concurrent 500 req/s spike load test; 4x duplicate out-of-order webhook replay; TTL expiration fault injection; DB pool regression check.
